feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: House could vote this week on articles of impeachment against Hegseth
entry.summary: The House is moving toward a vote this week on impeaching Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, after articles of impeachment were introduced Monday by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.

entry.title: TRUMP'S WEST TEXAS WALL
entry.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled Monday that the Trump administration can continue building a wall and other barriers in the Big Bend region in West Texas while litigation continues.

entry.title: Former Pentagon spokesman on articles of impeachment filed against Hegseth
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with former Pentagon spokesman John Ullyot about articles of impeachment brought against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.

entry.title: House GOP elects Jim Jordan as new leader as the party looks to rebuild from midterms
entry.summary: Jordan, a close Trump ally and co-founder of the ultra-conservative House Freedom Caucus, will succeed Mike Johnson, who says he's stepping down as the chamber's top Republican.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: The House could vote this week to impeach Pete Hegseth, Trump's shares mixed messaging on next steps in Iran, the investigation continues into Nvidia CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy.

entry.title: Actor John Malkovich talks about his new film, 'Wild Horse Nine'
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep talks to John Malkovich, who plays a grizzled CIA officer with a terminal illness and an axe to grind against the agency in the film "Wild Horse Nine."

entry.title: Kushner and Witkoff renew peace talks to end war between Russia and Ukraine
entry.summary: President Trump's top envoy is in Abu Dhabi with negotiators from Russia and Ukraine to resume peace talks.

entry.title: Trump's crypto profits raise alarms for transparency advocates
entry.summary: President Trump has made nearly $3 billion while in office, most of it in crypto ventures. And to the alarm of transparency advocates, much of the president's money comes from foreign sources.

entry.title: Swing voters share their thoughts on the election results
entry.summary: We hear from voters NPR has been following since before last week's midterm elections about what they want to see happen now.

entry.title: AI is making it harder to detect fake emergency calls
entry.summary: It's getting harder to detect fake emergency calls thanks to AI. The tech is being used to generate believable swatting calls to law enforcement that claim a shooting or other crime is taking place.
